summary: Nothing runs until a cue is started: by GO, a trigger (hotkey, MIDI, wall clock, timecode), another cue, OSC or AppleScript. A started cue runs its own action (play a file, fade, send a message) until it ends or is stopped; cues that are not running cost nothing beyond the list itself.
details: A single cue causes a single event when started [/fundamentals/cues/]
Cues continue until their programmed action ends or they are told to stop; running cues ignore extra starts by default [/fundamentals/cues/]
Load prepares a cue so it starts with minimum latency; QLab waits until every cue in a sequence is ready [/other-cues/transport-cues/]
Total cue count does not affect processor load; the number of simultaneously running cues does [/general/system-recommendations/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: In Max a message at a hot inlet makes an object compute (max_system_model.json dimension 1). In QLab there is no flow between cues at all; the unit of work is a whole cue, started by an event.

summary: Order is the list order plus continue modes and waits: GO starts the standing-by cue; auto-continue and auto-follow chain the next; Timeline groups order by pre-wait. Light commands inside a cue are applied top to bottom. Two cues started by one action start 'simultaneously' at human perception.
details: Auto-continue starts the next cue after the post-wait; auto-follow when the cue completes [/fundamentals/cue-sequences/]
Order of children inside a Timeline group does not matter; pre-waits do [/fundamentals/group-cues/]
Light cue commands are interpreted in order from top to bottom; Safe Sort leaves a command unsorted if moving it would change the result [/lighting/light-cues/]
The manual defines simultaneous as close enough for a person to perceive as simultaneous [/audio/introduction-to-audio/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max's depth-first, right-to-left message order (max_system_model.json dimension 2) has no counterpart; QLab's order is visible as rows and times, not as cord positions.
open_questions: Exact ordering of two cues started in the same instant is not documented.

summary: Times are seconds to the millisecond (shown to hundredths). Waits run on the system clock; cues with audio run on their audio device's clock and stay sample-locked within one output patch; video follows either the display or the audio clock. Timecode can be received (LTC/MTC) per list and generated by any number of Timecode cues. Rates 0.03 to 33 apply per cue; there is no tempo or metre (MIDI File cues are the exception).
details: All times precise to the millisecond, displayed to 0.01 or 0.1 s for performance [/fundamentals/inspector/]
Wait times use the system clock, not the audio device clock [/audio/introduction-to-audio/]
Video cue Clock: follow video clock or follow audio clock [/video/video-cues/]
QLab does not have a native concept of tempo and meter maps; MIDI File cues provide tempo-based timelines [/networking/midi-file-cues/]
Incoming timecode per list with lookback and freewheel; Timecode cues generate independent streams [/networking/using-timecode/, /networking/timecode-cues/]
Rate minimum 0.03, maximum 33 [/audio/audio-cues/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max has a tempo-aware transport and note-value times (max_system_model.json dimension 3); QLab has none, but it does have timecode in and out, which Max lacks as objects.

summary: No user-visible data flow. A cue's properties are typed fields (times, dB levels, text cue numbers, colours, curves, matrices of levels, 2D paths). Values cross to the outside world as OSC (strings, ints, floats, OSC 1.1 booleans, impulse, null), MIDI, MSC, DMX, timecode, audio and video.
details: Cue numbers are text strings; 1, 1.0 and 1.00 differ [/fundamentals/inspector/]
Levels are dBFS; unsigned entries are read as negative [/fundamentals/inspector/]
OSC formatting rules in Network cues, including \T \F \I \N [/networking/network-cues/]
OSC replies carry a JSON string [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max users think in messages, signals and matrices on cords (max_system_model.json dimension 4); QLab users think in properties of cues.

summary: Audio runs at the device rate with automatic sample-rate and bit-depth conversion per file; a cue uses up to 24 channels and a patch up to 128 cue outputs and 128 device outputs. Video runs at each output's refresh rate, with cues of any frame rate mixed on one stage. Network cues can resend at 1 to 120 fps; DMX frames go out about every 23 ms.
details: First 24 channels of a file are recognised; 8-192 kHz, 8-32 bit, converted on the fly [/audio/audio-cues/]
Patches: 1 to 128 cue outputs [/audio/audio-output-patch-editor/]
Cues with different frame rates can share a stage [/video/introduction-to-video/]
Resend fps menu from 1 to 120 [/networking/network-cues/]
A DMX frame every 23 ms or so [/lighting/introduction-to-lighting/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: No control rate exists to manage; Max's event/signal/frame split (max_system_model.json dimension 5) is hidden inside cue types.

summary: The workspace saves every cue property and all workspace settings. Runtime changes from Fade cues, Target cues and live OSC are temporary: not saved, not marked as edits, cleared by Reset. Autosave writes backup copies, never the workspace; a backup is kept before each manual save and rotated. Light definitions are embedded in the workspace.
details: Temporary properties are changes created by Target cues, Devamp cues or live OSC commands [/fundamentals/workspace/]
/live OSC forms change the live value without unsaved changes or undo [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
Reset returns the workspace to its just-opened state [/fundamentals/workspace/]
Backups and rotation [/fundamentals/workspace-settings/]
Definitions saved in the global library and embedded in the workspace [/lighting/introduction-to-lighting/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: A Max patch saves structure, not values (max_system_model.json dimension 6). QLab saves everything designed, and explicitly separates designed values from performance-time changes.

summary: Every cue setting is a fixed, named property of its cue type, reachable through the inspector, OSC (/cue/{n}/{property}) and AppleScript. Fade cues change chosen properties over time; there are no expressions or bindings between properties, except OSC queries in Network cues and light-command pulls.
details: Over 1,100 OSC methods covering cue and workspace properties [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
Increment/decrement syntax and live forms [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
OSC queries insert live values into outgoing messages [/scripting/osc-queries/]
Light commands can pull a value from another cue, scaled [/lighting/lighting-command-language/]
Workspace volume limits bound every level [/fundamentals/workspace-settings/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max attributes and Parameter Mode are per object and open-ended (max_system_model.json dimension 7); QLab's parameter set is closed but uniformly addressable by OSC.

summary: Group cues (five modes) are the only container. Reuse is by cue templates (default settings per cue type, including per-network-patch defaults), workspace templates, settings import/export, Paste Cue Properties presets, and Script cues that edit the workspace.
details: Group cue modes [/fundamentals/group-cues/]
Cue templates and workspace templates [/fundamentals/workspace-settings/, /fundamentals/workspace-templates/]
Network cue template per patch [/networking/network-cues/]
Paste Cue Properties presets [/tools/paste-cue-properties/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: No abstractions, arguments or instancing (max_system_model.json dimension 8); a QLab designer repeats structure by copying cues and templates.

summary: Cues are named by unique text cue numbers (workspace-wide) and permanent unique IDs; lists, patches, stages, routes and instruments have names. OSC addresses cues by number, selection, playhead or ID, with wildcards, and workspaces by name or ID; every workspace on a port receives unprefixed messages.
details: /cue/{x}, /cue/selected, /cue/playhead, /cue/*, /cue_id/{id} [/networking/using-osc/]
Cue IDs never change, even if name and number do [/networking/using-osc/]
Unprefixed workspace messages go to all workspaces on that port [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
Light instrument and group names: letters, numbers, spaces [/lighting/light-patch-editor/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max's global send/receive names (max_system_model.json dimension 9) are replaced by one workspace-wide namespace of cue numbers, used both by operators and by remote systems.

summary: The show is cue lists with playheads (sequential) and carts (non-sequential), containing cues and groups. Sequences are built from continue modes and Timeline groups; branching is limited to GoTo cues, Target cues, random groups and external triggers.
details: Cue list: the basic unit of sequential structure; cart: non-sequential [/]
GoTo cues move the playhead [/other-cues/goto-cues/]
Start Random groups [/fundamentals/group-cues/]
Inactive lists still respond to triggers [/fundamentals/cue-lists/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: This is the layer Max lacks (max_system_model.json dimension 10): QLab is almost nothing but show structure.

summary: One main window: GO button, standby display and notes (masthead), the cue list, and a tabbed inspector, plus secondary windows for other lists and carts, floating secondary inspectors, monitor windows, the Light Dashboard and a Workspace Status window. The operator interface is the cue list itself; remote interfaces are QLab Remote (iOS), Stream Deck and OSC.
details: Masthead: GO button, standby display, notes, toolbar [/fundamentals/workspace/]
Secondary inspectors float and stay on one cue [/fundamentals/inspector/]
Monitor windows for stages, inputs, auditions and maps [/tools/monitor-windows/]
QLab Remote and Stream Deck [/networking/qlab-remote/, /networking/stream-deck/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: There is no presentation view to design (max_system_model.json dimension 11): every QLab show looks the same to its operator, which is the point.

summary: Cues can be edited while running; level changes act live. Live fade preview (per workspace) makes edits to Fade cues audible while the target plays, or off to prepare fades blind. Light cues are edited 'blind' in the inspector, live in the Dashboard. Show mode locks editing. Collaborators edit on other Macs while cues run on the primary.
details: Levels tab adjustments take effect live [/audio/audio-cues/]
Integrated fade edits are heard only after restart [/audio/audio-cues/]
Live fade preview on or off [/tools/tools-menu/]
Light cue inspector edits are blind; Dashboard edits are live [/lighting/light-cues/]
Collaboration: last edit wins [/networking/collaboration/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Like Max, the show keeps running during edits (max_system_model.json dimension 12), but QLab adds explicit live-versus-blind choices that Max leaves to the patch author.

summary: AppleScript only, in Script cues (by default in a separate process) or from outside; a large AppleScript dictionary mirrors the OSC dictionary. Scripts mostly build and edit cues. OSC from Network cues back to QLab (localhost) plus queries is the other automation route.
details: Script cues run AppleScript; Run in separate process by default [/scripting/script-cues/]
AppleScript dictionary [/scripting/applescript-dictionary-v5/]
Examples: set levels, create fade-ins for selected cues [/scripting/examples/]
Network patch to localhost routes messages back into QLab with lowest latency [/fundamentals/workspace-settings/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: No JavaScript or object-building scripting (max_system_model.json dimension 13); scripting edits the document rather than defining new behaviour.

summary: Each cue knows if it is broken and why (red X with a tooltip); the Warnings tab lists broken cues, breaking and non-breaking warnings, disconnections and flags, with a help button to the matching manual section. Logs record triggers, MIDI in, OSC in and OSC out. Video Metrics show fps and render time per stage. A broken cue in a sequence still runs its timing.
details: Warnings tab categories and Open Help button [/tools/workspace-status-window/]
Logs tab: cue triggers, MIDI input, OSC input, OSC output [/tools/workspace-status-window/]
Video Metrics: FPS, target, render time [/tools/workspace-status-window/]
Broken cues keep sequence timing [/tools/workspace-status-window/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max reports to a console and leaves silent failures silent (max_system_model.json dimension 14); QLab validates every cue against its required settings before the show.

summary: A Metal video engine: cues draw on stages (up to 16384 x 16384) on 1001 layers with per-cue blend modes and video effects; stages are cut into regions, warped (perspective, linear, Bezier), masked by image, edge-blended, and sent through routes to displays, Blackmagic, Syphon or NDI.
details: Metal engine [/video/introduction-to-video/]
Layers, blend modes, video effects [/video/video-cues/]
Stage, region, route, device; masks; warping; edge blends [/video/video-output/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Jitter's open GL graph (max_system_model.json dimension 15) against a fixed 2D compositing pipeline with strong output mapping built in.

summary: The manual frames performance as hardware choice: processor load grows with running cues, media resolution and effects; GPU matters only for video. Script cues run in a separate process by default. Loading reduces start latency. Video Metrics and frame-time percentages expose render cost.
details: What does and does not cost processor power [/general/system-recommendations/]
Run in separate process [/scripting/script-cues/]
Render time as a percentage of a frame [/tools/workspace-status-window/]
Live OSC messages use less processing because they skip undo [/scripting/osc-dictionary-v5/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: No threads to configure (max_system_model.json dimension 16); a QLab user tunes media formats and the Mac instead.
open_questions: Threading inside QLab is not described.

summary: Collaboration (shared editing, cues run on the primary), OSC and MSC show control broadcast to follow or drive other systems, OSC control from other QLabs, timecode in and out, NDI and Syphon video, Dante/AVB audio through the OS.
details: Collaboration over LAN or VPN with permissions [/networking/collaboration/]
Show control broadcast /listen and /eventFormat [/networking/show-control-broadcast/]
Network patches with several destinations (primary and backup) [/networking/network-cues/]
NDI in and out [/video/using-ndi/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max builds networking from objects and has no shared-editing session (max_system_model.json dimension 17).

summary: Mac-only application, free to run with paid Audio, Video, Lighting (or Bundle) licences that unlock features; unlicensed cues using licensed features are broken. No standalone export or plug-in form. The workspace and its project folder are the deliverable; QLab Remote and Stream Deck extend control.
details: QLab 5 requires macOS 11 or later [/general/system-recommendations/]
Features by licence; demo mode 60 minutes [/general/features/]
License required warnings on cues [/audio/audio-cues/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max builds standalones, devices and RNBO exports (max_system_model.json dimension 18); QLab ships as the workspace plus a licensed copy of QLab.

summary: Users extend QLab with AudioUnit effects, light definitions (JSON), network device descriptions requested from Figure 53, AppleScript, OSC from other software, and templates. There is no SDK for new cue types in the pages read.
details: AudioUnits on cues, cue outputs and device outputs [/audio/audio-cues/, /audio/audio-output-patch-editor/]
Light definitions stored as .qlablight JSON files [/lighting/light-library/]
Network device descriptions added on request [/networking/network-cues/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max lets anyone write new objects in C, JS or gen (max_system_model.json dimension 19); QLab's cue types are fixed.
open_questions: No plug-in API for cue types was found in the manual.

summary: Cues target files directly; saving can create a project folder and copy every target into audio, video and midi subfolders, deduplicating identical files. A file target search tool relinks missing files. Fonts and AudioUnits are not copied. Collaboration remotes see only files inside the workspace folder.
details: Project folder and copy-on-target [/fundamentals/managing-workspaces/]
File target search tool [/tools/tools-menu/]
Fonts and AudioUnits cannot be copied [/fundamentals/managing-workspaces/]
Remotes see only files in the workspace folder [/networking/collaboration/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max finds files by search path and consolidates projects on request (max_system_model.json dimension 20); QLab gathers media into the show folder as you work.

dimension: The operator and the playhead (system-level because every way of starting a cue is defined by whether it moves the playhead)
summary: QLab assumes a human operator pressing GO. Each list's playhead is shared state that GO advances; triggers, Start cues, previews and OSC starts deliberately do not move it, GoTo cues and playhead commands do. Safety features (double-GO protection, panic, show mode, notes in the masthead) are built around that operator.
details: Starting via GO moves the playhead; hotkey, MIDI, timecode and wall clock triggers do not [/fundamentals/cue-sequences/]
Transport cues do not move the playhead; use GoTo [/other-cues/transport-cues/]
Lock playhead to selection option [/fundamentals/workspace-settings/]
Collaboration: the playhead is shared across collaborators [/networking/collaboration/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max has no notion of 'where the show is'. A Max show patch that copies QLab must decide which inputs advance the show position and which only fire actions.

dimension: Licences gate features in the same file (system-level because a workspace's behaviour depends on the licences of the machine that runs it)
summary: The same workspace runs differently with and without licences: without an Audio licence a cue uses only two channels and no effects; without a Video licence only one output device and no custom geometry; cues using unlicensed features are broken. In collaboration, every Mac behaves according to the primary's licences.
details: Features by licence table [/general/features/]
License required broken-cue reasons [/audio/audio-cues/, /video/video-cues/]
Collaboration sessions follow the primary's licence [/networking/collaboration/]
what_a_max_user_would_notice: Max's runtime and paid features do not change what a patch does on load in this way; worth knowing when comparing QLab's 'free' tier.
